title: Autopilot Apply: idempotent apply endpoints, SDK helpers, and webhook contracts for Optimize automation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Redwood Optimize will automatically propose batching and KV/prefix caching configuration changes to reduce per-token cost. We need a safe, auditable, and developer-friendly API + SDK + webhook contract that lets automation propose recommendations, apply them idempotently, and observe applies and rollbacks. Goals: 1) Provide idempotent apply semantics so retries and race conditions are safe; 2) Provide clear webhook events and statuses for downstream systems (Console, audits, metrics); 3) Offer an SDK wrapper to create, track, and safely revert applies; 4) Keep the control plane acceptance surface small and strictly validated to avoid regressions in production workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Public REST endpoints to create recommendation, propose an apply, confirm an apply, and request rollback exist and are documented
Applies are idempotent based on an 'apply_id' + 'resource_version' contract; duplicate requests are no-ops and return canonical result
Webhook events emitted for: recommendation.created, apply.attempt, apply.succeeded, apply.failed, apply.rolled_back with stable payload fields
SDK helpers in js/python provide: generateApplyId(), waitForApply(), safeRollback(), optimisticLock helpers
Audit trail is recorded: who triggered apply (automation service / user), pre/post config snapshots, diff, and cost/latency estimates
Automated canary rollout policy exists for Apply operations: canary percentage, monitoring window, automatic revert on regression
E2E integration tests covering retries, concurrent applies, rollback trigger, webhook fanout and replay semantics
Migration doc and Console UI hooks to show pending/active/reverted optimizations
implementation_notes:
Proposed REST surface (high level):
- POST /v1/optimize/recommendations  => create recommendation object (immutable)
  Payload: {recommendation_id, tenant_id, target_resource, changes, estimate_tokens_saved, rationale, proposer=automation-service, created_at}
- POST /v1/optimize/applies  => attempt to apply a recommendation
  Payload: {apply_id, recommendation_id, tenant_id, resource_version, canary_pct?, apply_strategy: [immediate|canary], idempotency_key}   Response: 202 accepted with apply_status
- GET /v1/optimize/applies/:apply_id => status and execution log
- POST /v1/optimize/applies/:apply_id/confirm => confirm continue after canary window
- POST /v1/optimize/applies/:apply_id/rollback => request rollback (idempotent)
Idempotency: server persists apply_id + final outcome. If identical apply_id + recommendation_id is received, return same response. If same apply_id but different payload, reject with 409. Use resource_version (server-side config generation hash) to ensure optimistic locking.
Webhook contract: event_type, timestamp, tenant_id, apply_id, recommendation_id, status, summary, links.audit, links.console. Webhook consumer must tolerate duplicate delivery and out-of-order receipts (include causal sequence numbers and a final "terminal" flag).
SDK: helpers will auto-generate RFC4122 v4 apply_id but allow caller-specified id. Provide exponential-backoff retry helper that preserves idempotency key. Provide convenience 'applyWithCanary' which posts apply, polls status, and confirms or rolls back based on configured thresholds.
Telemetry: emit metrics: apply_attempts_total, apply_success_total, apply_rollback_total, apply_latency_seconds, apply_conflicts_total. Tag by tenant, recommendation_type (batching|caching), and strategy.
